newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIA PALM OIL RISES ON WEAKER RUPIAH.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIA PALM OIL RISES ON WEAKER RUPIAH.

text.p: Indonesian palm oil prices rose in late trading on Thursday after the rupiah's steep plunge when the central bank scrapped its intervention band, traders said.
They said a tender was done at 1,285 rupiah/kg for 500 tonnes of palm oil in North Sumatran city of Medan in the afternoon against the last tender at 1,246 rupiah/kg on Tuesday.
Palm olein was slightly higher at 1,496-1,500 rupiah/kg in Jakarta.
"People are holding back positions because they want to wait for further developments in the currency," said one trader.

Bank Indonesia said it will no longer announce its daily intervention and conversion bands with immediate effect. Spot rupiah was ranging between 2,750 and 2,790 in the afternoon, with some players seen cashing out from dollars.
Spot rupiah fell to a low 2,800 in thin volume before recovering to 2,760/70 at 0810 GMT from an opening of 2,648/58.
Traders also said they largerly ignored the Malaysian palm oil output for July which was projected to to have risen 4.5 percent to 823,000 tonnes according to private forecaster Ivan Wong.
"Such figure has been widely expected so it does not have any impact on the Indonesian market," said one trader.

Traders said they expected to see some adjustment in palm olein prices on Friday after palm oil's rise. "At least olein prices should be quoted at 1,550, otherwise it will not be profitable to do business," said one trader.
